English Literature.question: ১) The character 'Brutus' is created by-
English Literature.exp:
Marcus Brutus, Roman general, one of the conspirators in Shakespeare’s Julius Caesar.
Though he is Caesar’s friend and a man of honour, Brutus joins in the conspiracy against Caesar’s life, convincing himself that Caesar’s death is for the greater good of Rome.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ২) Who wrote the poem 'To Daffodils'?
English Literature.exp:
Fair Daffodils, we weep to see
You haste away so soon;
As yet the early-rising sun
Has not attain'd his noon.
-To Daffodils
(Robert Herrick)

English Literature.question: ৩) Who is called the poet of love?
English Literature.exp:
John Donne, (born sometime between Jan. 24 and June 19, 1572, London, Eng. - died March 31, 1631, London), leading English poet of the Metaphysical school and dean of St. Paul’s Cathedral, London (1621–31).
Donne is often considered the greatest love poet in the English language.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৪) 'An Elegy Written in a Country Church Yard' is written by-
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Gray is an English poet whose “An Elegy Written in a Country Church Yard” is one of the best known of English lyric poems.
His other notable works-
'Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton', 'College', 'The Progress of Poesy', 'The Bard' etc.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৫) What kind of literary work 'The Jew of Malta' is?
English Literature.exp:
The Jew of Malta, in full The Famous Tragedy of the Rich Jew of Malta, five-act tragedy in blank verse by Christopher Marlowe, produced about 1590 and published in 1633.
His other famous literary works are-
Tamburlaine the Great Part I & II; Edward II; Doctor Faustus.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica

English Literature.question: ৬) Who is known for Compilation of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle?
English Literature.exp:
Alfred, byname Alfred the Great, (born 849 - died 899), king of Wessex (871–899), a Saxon kingdom in southwestern England.
He prevented England from falling to the Danes and promoted learning and literacy.
Compilation of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle began during his reign, circa 890.
Alfred considered learning and literacy to be crucial for the acquisition of wisdom and therefore necessary for men to live in accordance with God’s will.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question:
৭) “Where ignorance is bliss,
'Tis folly to be wise.” is a famous quotation by -
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Gray (1716 - 1771):
He is an English poet whose “An Elegy Written in a Country Church Yard” is one of the best known of English lyric poems.
He was the dominant poetic figure in the mid-18th century and a precursor of the Romantic movement.
Some of his quotes are-
-Where ignorance is bliss,
'Tis folly to be wise.
-Full many a flower is born to blush unseen,
And waste its sweetness on the desert air.
-Sorrow never comes too late.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৮) When did William Shakespeare die?
English Literature.exp:
William Shakespeare, byname Bard of Avon or Swan of Avon, (baptized April 26, 1564, Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire, England - died April 23, 1616, Stratford-upon-Avon).
He is an English poet, dramatist, and actor often called the English national poet and considered by many to be the greatest dramatist of all time.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question:
৯) Who stated the following line?
'A little learning is a dangerous thing.'
English Literature.exp:
Alexander Pope is poet and satirist of the English Augustan period, best known for his poems.
He is one of the most epigrammatic of all English authors.
His famous quotes are-
-To err is human, to forgive, divine.
-A little learning is a dangerous thing.
-An honest man's the noblest work of God.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ১০) 'Conquest of Granada' is a ____ written by John Dryden.
English Literature.exp:
The most popular writer of heroic plays was John Dryden, whose Conquest of Granada, in two parts (1670, 1671), had all the requisite elements of poetry, battle, courage, death, and murder.
His other notable works-
'Absalom and Achitophel', 'Mac Flecknoe', 'The Indian Emperor', 'Fables Ancient and Modern', 'The Indian Queen', 'The Wild Gallant'.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ১১) The religious allegory 'Pilgrim’s Progress' is written by-
English Literature.exp:
The Pilgrim’s Progress, religious allegory by the English writer John Bunyan, published in two parts in 1678 and 1684.
The work is a symbolic vision of the good man’s pilgrimage through life.
At one time second only to the Bible in popularity, The Pilgrim’s Progress is the most famous Christian allegory still in print.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ১২) ''Better to reign in Hell, then serve in Heav'n'' is quoted by-
English Literature.exp:
John Milton is best known for Paradise Lost, widely regarded as the greatest epic poem in English.
Some of his quotes from this epic are-
-To reign is worth ambition though in hell:
Better to reign in hell, than serve in heav'n.
-So farewell Hope, and with Hope farewell Fear,
Farewell Remorse: all Good to me is lost;
-Long is the way
And hard, that out of Hell leads up to light.
Evil be thou my Good.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ১৩) Who is the author of 'The Silent Women'?
English Literature.exp:
Ben Johnson: A neo-classicist though he wrote in the time when romantic mode of literature was prevalent.
He was called a neo-classicist because he followed the classical rules of drama.
His famous literary works are-
Every Man out of His Humour, Every Man in His Humour, Volpone, The Silent Women, The Alchemist.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ১৪) 'The Ecclesiastical History of the English People' is written by -
English Literature.exp:
St Bede, also known as the Venerable Bede, is widely regarded as the greatest of all the Anglo-Saxon scholars.
He wrote around 40 books mainly dealing with theology and history.
His most famous work, which is a key source for the understanding of early British history and the arrival of Christianity, is 'Historia Ecclesiastica Gentis Anglorum' or 'The Ecclesiastical History of the English People' which was completed in 731 AD.
Source: BBC

English Literature.question: ১৫) ‘Le Morte d'Arthur’ tells the story of -
English Literature.option2: খ) King Arthur and his Knights
English Literature.exp:
Le Morte Darthur, the first English-language prose version of the Arthurian legend, completed by Sir Thomas Malory about 1470 and printed by William Caxton in 1485.
Le Morte d'Arthur tells the story of King Arthur and his Knights at the Round Table.
Source: Britannica & Cliffsnotes

English Literature.question: ১৬) Who is a 'University Wit'?
English Literature.exp:
University wits are a group of young dramatists who wrote and performed in London towards the end of the 16th century during the Elizabethan Period.
They are called university wits because they were the witty students of Cambridge or Oxford.
Thomas Kyd, John Lyly, Robert Greene, George Peele, Christopher Marlowe and Thomas Nashe are university wits.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ১৭) Who is the writer of 'Euphues'?
English Literature.exp:
Euphues is a book written by John Lyly that bears the embryo of English novel.
John Lyly is a University Wit. His other famous works-
Campaspe, Sapho and Phao, Midas etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ১৮) Who wrote 'Essays'?
English Literature.exp:
Francis Bacon (1561-1626):
He wrote the book 'Essays' (1597). He is called the natural philosopher.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ১৯) 'Doctor Faustus’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Christopher Marlowe is a writer from the Elizabethan period. He is a university wit.
His famous literary works are-
Tamburlaine the Great Part I & II; The Jew of Malta; Edward II; Doctor Faustus.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr. M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২০) 'Astrophel and Stella' is a -
English Literature.exp:
Sir Philip Sidney, (born November 30, 1554, Penshurst, Kent, England—died October 17, 1586, Arnhem, Netherlands), Elizabethan courtier, statesman, soldier, poet, and patron of scholars and poets, considered the ideal gentleman of his day.
After Shakespeare's sonnets, Sidney's Astrophel and Stella is considered the finest Elizabethan sonnet cycle.
Note that, 'Astrophel' is a poem by Edmund Spenser.
Source: Britannica & Goodreads

English Literature.question: ২১) Who is the writer of ‘The Spanish Tragedy’?
English Literature.exp:
'The Spanish Tragedy' is written by Thomas Kyd.
Thomas Kyd, English dramatist who, with his The Spanish Tragedy (sometimes called Hieronimo, or Jeronimo, after its protagonist), initiated the revenge tragedy of his day. He was a university wit.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ২২) Who wrote the first English tragedy?
English Literature.exp:
Gorboduc, play by Thomas Norton and Thomas Sackville that takes as its subject Gorboduc, a mythical king of ancient Britain.
It is the first English tragedy.
Source: Britannica and An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৩) Who is called the poet of poets in English Literature?
English Literature.exp:
Edmund Spenser is known as the 'Poet of Poets' in English literature because many later English poets followed his art of poetry.
His literary works -
The Faerie Queene (1590), The Shepherd's Calendar (1579).
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৪) ‘Utopia' is a famous work of -
English Literature.exp:
Utopia (or Kingdom of Nowhere) is a famous book of Thomas More.
The book was originally written in Latin in 1516.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৫) Which of the following books is written by William Shakespeare?
English Literature.exp:
William Shakespeare (1564-1616):
The greatest English dramatist, famous for the objective presentation of his deep knowledge about human psychology.
He is often called the bard of Avon. His literary works are-
The Comedy of Errors, Love's Labour's Lost, Romeo and Juliet, King John, The Merchant of Venice, Julius Caesar, As You Like It, Hamlet etc.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৬) Who wrote the famous allegorical work 'Piers Plowman'?
English Literature.exp:
William Langland, (born c. 1330 - died c. 1400), presumed author of one of the greatest examples of Middle English alliterative poetry, generally known as Piers Plowman, an allegorical work with a complex variety of religious themes.
Source: britannica

English Literature.question: ২৭) The poem 'Juliana' is written by-
English Literature.exp:
Cynewulf, also spelled Cynwulf or Kynewulf, (flourished 9th century AD, Northumbria or Mercia [now in England]), author of four Old English poems preserved in late 10th-century manuscripts.
Juliana, a poem of 731 lines, is a retelling of a Latin prose life of St. Juliana, a maiden who rejected the suit of a Roman prefect, Eleusius, because of her faith and consequently was made to suffer numerous torments.
Source: britannica

English Literature.question: ২৮) Who translated 'The Bible' into English from Latin?
English Literature.exp:
John Wycliffe(1324-1384) translated The Bible into English from Latin.
He is called the father of English prose.
Source: An ABC of English Literature, Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ২৯) Who is the author of 'The Canterbury Tales'?
English Literature.exp:
Geoffrey Chaucer (1340-1400): The outstanding English poet before Shakespeare.
His 'The Canterbury Tales' ranks as one of the greatest poetic works in English.
His other notable works-
'Troilus and Criseyde', 'The Parlement of Foules', 'The Pardoner’s Tale', 'The Miller’s Tale', 'The Friar’s Tale', 'The Nun’s Priest’s Tale', 'The Clerk’s Tale', 'The Man of Law’s Tale', 'The Franklin’s Tale'.
Source: britannica

English Literature.question: ৩০) Who wrote 'A dictionary of the English Language'?
English Literature.exp:
Samuel Johnson:
English critic, biographer, essayist, poet, and lexicographer, regarded as one of the greatest figures of 18th-century life and letters.
A Dictionary of the English Language is the famous dictionary of Samuel Johnson, published in London in 1755;
its principles dominated English lexicography for more than a century.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩১) Which of the following is a novel?
English Literature.exp:
Tom Jones, in full The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling, comic novel by Henry Fielding, published in 1749.
Tom Jones is constructed around a romance plot.
The Gift of Magi, To Build a Fire and Eve's Diary are short stories written by O. Henry, Jack London and Mark Twain.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩২) ‘Robinson Crusoe’ was written by -
English Literature.exp:
Daniel Defoe, English novelist, pamphleteer, and journalist.
Robinson Crusoe, is a novel by Daniel Defoe, first published in London in 1719.
Defoe’s first long work of fiction, it introduced two of the most-enduring characters in English literature: Robinson Crusoe and Friday.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩৩) Who is the author of 'Gulliver’s Travels'?
English Literature.exp:
Jonathan Swift, Anglo-Irish author, who was the foremost prose satirist in the English language.
His notable works-
'Gulliver’s Travels', 'A Tale of a Tub', 'Journal to Stella', 'A Modest Proposal' etc.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩৪) Find the odd one out.
English Literature.exp:
Sir Thomas Malory, Geoffrey Chaucer and John Wycliffe are from The Middle English Period.
George Peele is from The Elizabethan Age.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৩৫) John Gower is famous for -
English Literature.option3: গ) The Jew of the Malta
English Literature.exp:
John Gower, medieval English poet in the tradition of courtly love and moral allegory, whose reputation once matched that of his contemporary and friend Geoffrey Chaucer, and who strongly influenced the writing of other poets of his day.
His is famous for ‘Confessio Amantis’.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩৬) ‘Ralph Roister Doister’ is a -
English Literature.exp:
Nicholas Udall, English playwright, translator, and schoolmaster who wrote the first known English comedy, Ralph Roister Doister.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩৭) Who wrote “The Old Wives’ Tale”?
English Literature.exp:
George Peele, (born c. July 25, 1556, London, England - died c. November 9, 1596), Elizabethan dramatist who experimented in many forms of theatrical art: pastoral, history, melodrama, tragedy, folk play, and pageant.
Notable Works:
“The Arraignment of Paris”
“The Old Wives’ Tale”
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৩৮) Thomas Nashe wrote -
English Literature.option1: ক) The Life of Jack Wilton
English Literature.option3: গ) The Taming of the Shrew
English Literature.exp:
Thomas Nashe, poet, dramatist, and author of The Unfortunate Traveller; or, The Life of Jack Wilton (1594), the first picaresque novel in English.
Source: Britannica.com

English Literature.question: ৩৯) Who is the author of ‘The Teares of Peace’?
English Literature.exp:
George Chapman, English poet and dramatist, whose translation of Homer long remained the standard English version.
The first books of his translation of the Iliad appeared in 1598. It was completed in 1611, and his version of the Odyssey appeared in 1616.
Chapman’s Homer contains passages of great power and beauty and inspired the sonnet of John Keats “On First Looking into Chapman’s Homer” (1815).
His notable works are: “Bussy d’Ambois”
“Euthymiae Raptus; or the Teares of Peace”
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৪০) Who wrote ‘The White Devil’?
English Literature.exp:
John Webster is a writer of The Jacobean Period.
His notable works are:
The White Devil (1612)
The Duchess of Malfi.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪১) ‘The Atheist’s Tragedy’ is written by which author?
English Literature.exp:
Cyril Tourneur is a writer of The Jacobean Period.
His notable works are:
The Revenger’s Tragedy
The Atheist’s Tragedy.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪২) Whose famous literary work is “Easter Wings”?
English Literature.exp:
George Herbert, English religious poet, a major metaphysical poet, notable for the purity and effectiveness of his choice of words.
“Easter Wings” is his famous literary work.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৪৩) Andrew Marvell’s notable work -
English Literature.exp:
Andrew Marvell, English poet whose political reputation overshadowed that of his poetry until the 20th century.
He is now considered to be one of the best Metaphysical poets.
His notable works are:
“To His Coy Mistress”
“The Rehearsal Transpros’d”.
The Dunciad is a poem by Alexander Pope.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৪৪) ‘Hudibras’ is a -
English Literature.exp:
Samuel Butler is a writer from The Restoration Period.
He is famous for his satiric poem ‘Hudibras’.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪৫) William Congreve is a writer from -
English Literature.exp:
William Congreve is a writer from The Restoration Period.
His notable works are:
The Double Dealer
Love for Love
The Way of The World.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪৬) Who wrote ‘The Beaux’s Stratagem’?
English Literature.exp:
George Farquhar is a writer from The Restoration Period.
His notable works are:
The Recruiting Officer
The Beaux’s Stratagem.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪৭) 'Go, lovely Rose!' is a poem by -
English Literature.exp:
Edmund Waller, (born March 3, 1606, Coleshill, Hertfordshire, Eng. - died Oct. 21, 1687, Beaconsfield, Buckinghamshire), English poet whose adoption of smooth, regular versification prepared the way for the heroic couplet’s emergence by the end of the century as the dominant form of poetic expression.
Several of Waller’s poems, including “Go, lovely Rose!” - one of the most famous lyric poems in English literature.
Source: Britannica

English Literature.question: ৪৮) Which of the following writers are from The Age of Sensibility?
English Literature.exp:
Major writers of The Age of Sensibility: Samuel Richardson, Samuel Johnson, Henry Fielding, Thomas Grey, Oliver Goldsmith, Edmund Burke, Edward Gibbon.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৪৯) ‘The Vicar of Wakefield’ is written by -
English Literature.exp:
Oliver Goldsmith (1728 - 74) is a writer from The Age of Sensibility.
His famous works are:
The Citizen of the World
The Vicar of Wakefield.
Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman

English Literature.question: ৫০) What kind of literary work is ‘The Duchess of Malfi’?
English Literature.exp:
The Duchess of Malfi, five-act tragedy by English dramatist John Webster, performed 1613/14 and published in 1623.
The Duchess of Malfi tells the story of the spirited duchess and her love for her trustworthy steward Antonio. She was eventually betrayed by Bosola, a spy.
Webster’s The Duchess of Malfi is often regarded as the last great tragedy of the Elizabethan and Jacobean eras, second only to William Shakespeare’s.
Source: Britannica
